title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables n, i, j: constant → O(1)
- no containers allocated
- no recursion
- not counted: input vector nums (modified in place)
approach: Since the array is sorted, all duplicates of a value are adjacent. Use two pointers: a write pointer `i` marking where the next unique element goes, and a read pointer `j` scanning the array. Whenever `nums[j]` differs from `nums[j-1]`, it is a new unique value, so copy it to `nums[i]` and advance `i`. The first element is always unique, so `i` starts at 1. Return `i`, which equals the count of unique elements.
hints: When the array is sorted in non-decreasing order, where do all copies of the same value end up relative to each other? The constraints guarantee nums is sorted.
Use two pointers: a write pointer `i` and a read pointer `j`. On [1,1,2], j=1 sees nums[1]==nums[0] so skip; j=2 sees nums[2]!=nums[1] so write nums[i=1]=2 and i becomes 2.

**Smallest input** - only one element, the loop body never runs.
`Input: nums = [5]` → `Expected: 1, nums = [5]`
⚠️ Bug: initialising the write pointer at 0 and returning it without counting the first element → returns 0

**All elements equal** - every value is identical, so only one unique element exists.
`Input: nums = [7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: 1, nums = [7,_,_,_]`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing `i` before writing (`i++; nums[i]=nums[j]`) skips recording the first unique value → returns 0

**No duplicates** - every element is already distinct.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3]` → `Expected: 3, nums = [1,2,3]`
⚠️ Bug: returning `i-1` (off-by-one) → returns 2

**Negatives and zeros** - values span negative, zero, positive.
`Input: nums = [-3,-1,0,0,2]` → `Expected: 4, nums = [-3,-1,0,2,_]`
⚠️ Bug: comparing with `<` instead of `!=` against the previous element and relying on sign → misses zero-vs-zero equality, returns 5

followUps.q: What if the input array is NOT sorted?
followUps.a: Duplicates are no longer adjacent, so the adjacent-scan two-pointer misses them. Use a hash set to record seen values; write each unseen value at the write pointer. Time stays O(n), but space becomes O(n).

followUps.q: What if each unique value may appear at most twice (generalised to k copies)?
followUps.a: Keep the same two-pointer shape but write `nums[j]` only when `nums[j] != nums[i-2]` (for k=2). Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the input is an unbounded sorted stream that cannot fit in memory?
followUps.a: Keep only the last emitted value and a counter; emit when the incoming value changes. Single pass, O(1) space, but requires the stream to remain sorted.
